claim: Sounion archaeological site costs €20 in summer, opens 09:30 to sunset, and the KTEL bus leaves from opposite Pedion tou Areos near Victoria metro, taking about 2 hours for €6.30 one way.
quote: Temple of Poseidon tickets cost 20 euro ... from 9:30 to sunset ... from a bus stop opposite Pedion tou Areos, close to Victoria metro station on the green line ... A one-way ticket costs €6.30.

claim: Cape Sounion is a 1-1.5 hour drive with almost no shade at the site; summer sunset falls around 20:15-20:45 and organised half-day sunset tours run €50-70.
quote: There is almost zero shade at the site. Zero.

claim: Four daily KTEL buses run Athens (Liosion) to Delphi, about 3 hours each way, €33 return, leaving roughly 4 hours on site; Delphi opens 08:00-20:00 April-October and costs €20.
quote: There are normally four buses every day that leave from the KTEL station at Liosion in northern Athens. The trip takes about three hours and you'll be able to spend about four hours in Delphi before the next return.

claim: The direct Athens-Kalambaka train is suspended until late 2026/mid-2027, leaving a 4h30 €54 express bus, and the author advises against attempting Meteora as a day trip.
quote: Direct Athens-Kalambaka train service is suspended until late 2026/mid-2027. ... I personally wouldn't do it. It really doesn't leave enough time to enjoy the UNESCO-listed Meteora Monasteries, and it's a LONG day!

claim: Each Meteora monastery costs €5 cash, closes on a different weekday, and several shut by 15:00-16:00 even in the summer schedule.
quote: €5 per person per monastery, payable in cash at the monastery entrance. ... Great Meteoro 09:30–15:00, Closed on Tuesdays ... Holy Trinity 10:00–16:00, Closed Thursdays

claim: The three-island cruise runs about 11 hours (07:00-18:00) for €110-130 with only 1h at Poros, 1.5h at Hydra and 2h at Aegina, versus ~€30 each way by hydrofoil for 6-7 hours on Hydra alone.
quote: Poros 1 hour free time ... Hydra, 1.5 hours free time ... Aegina, 2 hours free time ... You're not going to deeply explore any single island. ... 6-7 hours on the island instead of 1.5. Worth it if Hydra is your priority.

claim: Travellers who did the three-island cruise report roughly an hour ashore per island, heavy onboard smoking on the open deck, and recommend a single island instead.
quote: It appears you'll spend more time on a boat than actual time on each island. ... the scenic back of the boats are where the smokers are allowed to smoke so consider where you sit ... yes it was non-stop smoking

claim: Piraeus-Hydra crossings take 1h05 to just over 2h with up to 12 daily sailings operated by Alpha Lines, Hellenic Seaways and Magic Sea Ferries.
quote: 1 hr 5 min to just over 2 hr ... Alpha Lines, Hellenic Seaways, and Magic Sea Ferries ... high-speed catamarans

claim: Piraeus-Aegina takes 40 minutes to 1h25 for €11.50-19.50, with at least 9 daily high-speed connections plus 5+ conventional sailings.
quote: from a minimum of 40 minutes to a maximum of 1 hour and 25 minutes ... between €11.50 and €19.50 ... at least 9 daily connections

claim: Piraeus-Poros runs up to 6 daily crossings, 55 minutes to over 2.5 hours, from €17 one way.
quote: The trip duration ranges from 55 min to over 2.5 hr ... up to 6 daily crossings ... Ticket prices start at €17

claim: Aegina's bus network runs from the port for €1.80-2.00 per ticket, with 8 daily services on the Agia Marina line that passes the Temple of Aphaia — though some departures skip it.
quote: a one-way ticket is priced between 1.80 EUR and 2.00 EUR ... 8 routes per day ... Some buses follow an alternative route that doesn't pass by Mesagros and the Temple of Aphaia.

claim: The Proastiakos to New Corinth takes about 1.5 hours, then a €10-12 taxi covers the 7 km to the site (€8 including museum, 08:00-20:00 summer); Acrocorinth has no shade.
quote: The Proastiakos (suburban rail) runs from Athens to the town of Kiato, stopping in New Corinth. The ride takes about 1.5 hours. ... From New Corinth station, you'll need a taxi to the archaeological site (about 7 km, ~€10-12). ... It's exposed. No shade inside the fortress

claim: Mycenae and Epidaurus are 2-2.5 hours from Athens, €12 summer combined ticket each, open 08:00-19:30 April-October; guided full-day tours run 10-12 hours at €85-130 and both sites are exposed at 35°C+ in July-August.
quote: 120 km southwest, 2-2.5 hours by car via the Athens-Corinth motorway. ... €12 standard summer / €6 winter combined ticket ... Both sites are mostly exposed; bring water, sun hat, and sunscreen. ... July-August: hot (often 35°C+ at both sites), peak crowds.

claim: KTEL Argolidas buses link Athens Kifissos and Nafplio in roughly 2 hours for about €15-19.
quote: Bus Náfplio to Athens from $15

claim: Kaisariani Monastery opens 08:30-16:00 daily except Tuesdays, costs €3, needs 1-2 hours, and is reachable by bus 224 from Syntagma plus a 40-minute uphill walk or a ~€10 taxi.
quote: Open every day except Tuesdays from 8:30-16:00 ... hop on a 224 bus from the Syntagma square and get off at the last stop, after which there is a 40-minute walk up Mount Hymettus to the monastery ... You will need anything between 1 and 2 hours for the walled complex

claim: Daphni Monastery, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, opens 08:00-16:00 Tuesday to Sunday, closed Mondays, €6 for adults.
quote: The monastery is open from 8:00 AM to 4:00 PM, Tuesday to Sunday. It's closed on Mondays. ... The entrance fee is €6 for adults.

claim: Rhamnous is ~50 km and about an hour by car, open 08:30-15:30 closed Tuesdays, €5, and by public transport requires a KTEL bus to Marathon town plus a ~€15 taxi for the last 15 km.
quote: 08:30-15:30 daily, closed Tuesdays ... 5 EUR (full), reduced rates available ... take a KTEL bus to Marathon town (around 4 EUR, 1 hour 20 minutes), then taxi the remaining 15 km (roughly 15 EUR one way)

claim: Vravrona is about a 30-minute drive from Athens, €6 in main season including the museum, and closes at 15:30; bus 304 from Nomismatokopio takes over an hour and stops 2 km short.
quote: The drive from Athens only takes around half an hour ... There is an entrance fee of 3 euros during the winter or 6 through the main season including entrance to both the archaeological site a museum. The site closes at 15:30.

claim: The Marathon tomb and museum open 08:30-15:30 and are reached by KTEL Attikis bus in 1-1.5 hours, but visitors report the site is essentially just the tumulus.
quote: 8:30 AM–3:30 PM ... typically takes around 1 to 1.5 hours, depending on traffic ... you have the hill (tumulus)….and nothing more.

claim: Lake Vouliagmeni charges €17 weekdays and €19 weekends/holidays for general admission, opens 08:00-19:00 in summer, with sunbed sets an extra €40-90 for two.
quote: adult general admission at EUR 17 on weekdays and EUR 19 on weekends or holidays ... Lounge chair set (2 guests): €40 weekdays / €50 weekends ... Sunbed set (2 guests): €70 weekdays / €90 weekends

claim: Tram T3 reaches Glyfada in 35-45 minutes and Voula in 50-60 minutes from Syntagma on a €1.20 90-minute integrated ticket, with free public beaches at Edem, Kalamaki and parts of Glyfada; Lake Vouliagmeni needs a bus 122 transfer at Asklipieio Voulas.
quote: €1.20 single (90-minute integrated ticket valid on Metro, bus, and tram). ... Glyfada: 35-45 minutes ... Voula: 50-60 minutes ... Tram T3 to Asklipieio Voulas terminus (55-65 minutes from Syntagma), then transfer to bus 122

claim: Greece's July 2026 heatwave peaked at 43.5°C on 22 July, with wildfires near Athens on 2 August mostly contained by 4 August.
quote: 43.5 °C was reached on 22 July 2026 ... Fires affected the islands of Kefalonia and the village of Psatha near Athens on 2 August ... The Greek fires had mostly been contained by 4 August

claim: On extreme-heat days the Greek Culture Ministry closes the Acropolis and other archaeological sites roughly midday to 17:00, and forecasters expect August 2026 to run hotter than July across Greece.
quote: Forecasters expect August 2026 to run hotter than July across Greece. ... during the peak heatwave period, closures typically occurred from midday to 5pm on extreme-heat days ... EMY, the Hellenic National Meteorological Service, issues the forecasts and heat warnings

claim: A Hydra day trip on the 07:30/08:00 hydrofoil returning 17:00/18:30 yields 7-8 hours on a fully car-free island for €60-120 per person all-in, with water taxis €8-15 to nearby beaches.
quote: Hydra is completely car-free. No cars, no motorbikes, no scooters. ... 5:00 or 6:30 PM ferry ... €60-120 per person (ferry round trip + lunch + water taxi to a beach) ... one of the best day trips you can do from Athens

claim: Organised Delphi day tours run 8-10 hours, depart 07:00-08:30 from Syntagma or Omonia, cost €32.76-84 per person and cover the 2.5-hour each-way drive plus site and museum entry.
quote: €32.76 to €84, depending on inclusions and upgrades ... 8 to 10 hours, depending on tour type ... depart between 7 and 8:30am from Syntagma or Omonia Square ... about 2.5 hours each way
